subject.title: chore(pr): reuse green hosted CI from patch-identical pre-rebase heads

question: Should hosted-CI reuse accept whitespace-insensitive patch equivalence, or must the reusable patch comparison preserve whitespace for all repository files?
rationale: This choice changes the integrity boundary of a merge gate: patch-ID matching can reuse green CI for a head whose whitespace-only changes are behaviorally significant in formats such as YAML or indentation-sensitive code.

options.title: Preserve byte-sensitive patch changes
options.body: Replace the reuse comparison with a rebase-tolerant comparison that preserves whitespace, then add a whitespace-different rejection case and real prepare-run proof.

options.title: Accept whitespace-insensitive reuse
options.body: Keep `git patch-id --stable` only with an explicit maintainer decision that this CI-gate tradeoff is acceptable for every file type covered by the gate.

options.title: Pause the reuse feature
options.body: Keep the exact-head hosted-CI requirement until a safe equivalence contract and upgrade-proof path are agreed.

recommendation.title: Preserve byte-sensitive patch changes
recommendation.body: Replace the reuse comparison with a rebase-tolerant comparison that preserves whitespace, then add a whitespace-different rejection case and real prepare-run proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current contributor owns the proposed CI-gate contract and can supply its intended operational boundary; prior-area ownership could not be established from the supplied read-only evidence.
